newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin sports supremo sacked - TV report.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin sports supremo sacked - TV report.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has sacked his tennis coach from two powerful posts in the Kremlin sports administration, ORT state television said on Saturday, adding that the official had been linked to recent scandals.

Quoting an unnamed source, the station said Shamil Tarpishchev was also resigning from the International Olympic Committee because "scandals recently linked to his name may damage international reputation of Russian sport".
It did not specify the scandals. Russian media have speculated on possible financial irregularities involving a national sports funding body supervised by Tarpishchev.
Kremlin officials could not be reached for comment.
Tarpishchev's political rise began when he regularly played tennis with Yeltsin before the 65-year-old president developed the heart trouble for which he is now planning to have bypass surgery.

ORT said Yeltsin had dismissed Tarpishchev from both his official Kremlin posts -- chairman of the State Committee on Sports and Tourism and chairman of the Presidential Coordinating Committee on Sports and Tourism.

In these capacities, Tarpishchev oversaw the operations of the National Sports Foundation, a wealthy body which uses a lucrative special tax concession to import alcohol and tobacco and channel the profits into sport.

The agency's head, Boris Fyodorov, was accused of possessing drugs in May and then left gravely ill after a shooting and knife attack in June. Russia media said the attack was aimed at stopping him disclosing financial irregularities at the Fund.
Tarpishchev was close to Alexander Korzhakov, Yeltsin's chief bodyguard and close friend, who was sacked with other hawkish aides shortly after the first round of the presidential election in June.
After his reelection Yeltsin appointed Anatoly Chubais, a foe of Korzhakov, to run the Kremlin administration.
